descriptionChirho: Basic motion from one place to another, departing or traveling; the primary Qal sense of directed movement rendered in Arabic as ذَهَبَ (dhahaba) and in Korean as 가다 (gada).

Walking in a path or way of life, moral conduct or lifestyle; distinguished by Arabic سَلَكَ (salaka) and يَمْشِي (yamshi), Korean 걷다 (geotda), and Swahili kutembea, often used with 'in the ways/statutes of'.
Idiomatic invitation or summons meaning 'come!' or 'come now!'; rendered in Arabic as تَعَالَ (ta'ala) or هَلُمَّ (halumma), Korean 오라 (ora), and Swahili njoo/njooni.
Hifil causative sense: to lead, guide, drive, or bring someone somewhere; Arabic قَادَ/سَاقَ, Korean 인도하다/데려가다, Swahili kuongoza/kupeleka.
Emphatic departure or going away with finality, vanishing or passing away; the sense of permanent removal or disappearance, often of life or things ceasing.
